Modified assessment using the Beige Book as context: The FOMC held the target range at 4.25–4.50%, kept balance‑sheet reduction on a modest path (small Treasury runoff cap, MBS reinvestments into Treasuries), and maintained IORB at 4.4%. The latest Beige Book points to broadly modest-to-flat activity, softer consumer spending in discretionary categories, continued weakness in CRE (especially office) and subdued residential real estate, easing labor demand with moderating wage growth, and slower but still above-target price increases. Contacts also reported tight credit conditions and cautious risk appetite among lenders. These Beige Book signals reinforce the SLOOS evidence of tight supply of credit and weak loan demand, implying additional private‑sector restraint on growth beyond the policy rate and a gradual easing in price pressures.

Together with elevated outlook uncertainty and two dovish dissents favoring a 25 bp cut, the Beige Book steers the overall policy tone slightly more dovish than a SLOOS‑only read. The Committee’s pause and balanced risk language remain appropriate, but incoming anecdotal evidence tilts risks toward weaker growth with incremental disinflation.
